title: SafeCRS: Personalized Safety Alignment for LLM-Based Conversational Recommender Systems

problem.claim: LLM-based conversational recommender systems may produce recommendations that violate personalized safety constraints inferred from user conversations.

gap.claim: Current systems primarily optimize recommendation accuracy and user satisfaction without adequately respecting individualized safety sensitivities.

contributions.claim: SafeRec is a benchmark dataset for evaluating safety risks in LLM-based conversational recommender systems under user-specific constraints.
SafeCRS is a safety-aware training framework combining Safe-SFT and Safe-GDPO to jointly optimize recommendation quality and personalized safety alignment.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe SafeRec as a new benchmark dataset and SafeCRS as a proposed framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors find that SafeCRS achieves up to a 96.5% reduction in safety violation rates versus the strongest recommendation-quality baseline, while preserving competitive recommendation quality.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing LLM-based conversational recommender systems primarily optimize recommendation accuracy and user satisfaction.
Recommendation outputs can violate personalized safety constraints inferred from conversations.
The paper introduces SafeRec to evaluate safety risks under user-specific constraints.
The paper proposes SafeCRS, combining Safe-SFT and Safe-GDPO for recommendation quality and safety alignment.
The authors report lower safety violation rates with competitive recommendation quality.

source_observation.claim: Safety constraints may be individualized and implicitly inferred from conversational context.

interpretation.claim: Conversational recommender evaluation should account for user-specific safety sensitivities rather than only aggregate quality.

application.claim: Use constraint-aware benchmarks and training objectives when deploying recommendation systems in sensitive user contexts.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how personalized constraints are inferred or how safety performance generalizes beyond the reported setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset composition, evaluation protocols, or baseline details.
The abstract does not report the absolute safety violation rates or recommendation-quality metrics.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility of the reported results.
